segments.line: By day five, the city changes.
People stop sharing.
Shop windows get smashed. The
man across the street, who never says hello, now sits in front of
his garage with a baseball bat. His garage is full of canned food. And
nobody's coming to help. Radios are dead. Phones are dead. The
government can't call anyone, so it can't tell anyone anything. The
only news travels on foot. A rumor says the
army is handing out food downtown.
Another says it's the same all over the world.
Only one of them is true.
Far away, a much bigger problem is starting. Even switched off, the
fuel in a nuclear reactor keeps making heat, and it needs pumps to stay cool. In
2011, at Fukushima, the backup power failed, and
three reactors melted down. That's real.
Now there are more than four hundred reactors on Earth, and not one working pump.
Somewhere, engineers are fighting to cool them with gravity, buckets and courage. At
home, your mom counts what's left.
Six cans of beans. Half a bag of rice. Twelve bottles of water.
Five days, if you're careful. That
night, someone knocks on the door. It's the
man with the bat. He saw your water bottles through the window.
'I've got food, ' he says. 'You've got water. Let's talk. ' Your mom
looks at you. Then at Ellie. Then back at him.
'Half, ' she says. 'Half our water, for half your food. '
He thinks about it for a long time. Then he nods.
